source.semantic_boundary: Reference metadata only. A wiki entry, example, predicted domain or description does not validate a query protein, assign a catalytic role, establish system completeness, or change accepted analysis results.

systems.title: Abi2
systems.mechanism_summary: The page groups AbiD, AbiD1 and AbiF under Abi2. It describes phage-triggered AbiD1 toxicity and interference with a phage endonuclease, while also retaining a general unresolved-mechanism statement.

systems.title: AbiA
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiA has large and small forms; the small-form example includes a SLATT partner. The wiki leaves the molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: AbiB
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiB activation during infection is associated with extensive messenger RNA loss. Recognition of an early phage protein is proposed, but the activating protein and interaction remain unresolved.

systems.title: AbiC
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiC is a one-protein system classified as abortive infection in the cited overview. The wiki provides no resolved molecular mechanism.

systems.title: AbiD
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiD/F defenses involve regulated ribonuclease toxicity. The page describes RNA antitoxin control of AbiF and phage-triggered AbiD1 activity; these related systems should not be treated as one identical mechanism.

systems.title: AbiE
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiE pairs a growth-inhibiting, GTP-binding nucleotidyltransferase toxin with a transcriptional repressor antitoxin. The proteins are described as a type IV toxin–antitoxin pair without direct toxin–antitoxin binding.

systems.title: AbiG
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiG contains AbiGi and AbiGii and is classified as abortive infection in the cited overview. Its molecular mechanism remains unresolved on the wiki.

systems.title: AbiH
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiH is a one-protein defense with no resolved molecular mechanism. The page explicitly leaves its abortive-infection phenotype uncertain.

systems.title: AbiI
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiI is a one-protein defense classified as abortive infection in the cited overview; the wiki leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: AbiJ
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiJ is a one-protein defense with similarity to AbiC. Its molecular mechanism remains unresolved on the wiki.

systems.title: AbiK
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiK belongs to the reverse-transcriptase-containing UG/Abi group. The page describes abortive-infection activity but leaves the molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: AbiL
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiL comprises AbiLi and AbiLii. The page describes abortive-infection protection and loss of resistance after an AbiLii deletion, without establishing a complete molecular mechanism.

systems.title: AbiN
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiN is a one-protein system. Both the molecular mechanism and assignment of an abortive-infection phenotype remain unresolved on the wiki.

systems.title: AbiO
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiO is a one-protein defense containing a helicase domain. Abortive infection is proposed, but the page does not resolve its mechanism.

systems.title: AbiP2
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiP2 is a reverse-transcriptase-containing UG/Abi defense associated with P2-like phages. The page distinguishes it from AbiP and leaves its mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: AbiQ
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiQ is a ribonuclease restrained by the antiQ RNA antitoxin. The page describes this type III toxin–antitoxin interaction but leaves infection-dependent activation unresolved.

systems.title: AbiR
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiR contains AbiRa, AbiRb and AbiRc. Predicted transcription-associated, nuclease-like and ATPase domains are described, but the wiki does not establish the defense mechanism.

systems.title: AbiT
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiT contains AbiTi and AbiTii, with a transmembrane region reported for AbiTi. Its molecular mechanism remains unresolved on the wiki.

systems.title: AbiU
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiU expression is associated with delayed phage transcription. The page also notes a nearby candidate defense inhibitor, while leaving the causal protection mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: AbiV
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiV is a one-protein defense containing a HEPN domain. The wiki classifies it as abortive infection but leaves the molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: AbiZ
systems.mechanism_summary: AbiZ responds to phage lysis proteins and advances host-cell lysis, interrupting phage production through abortive infection.

systems.title: Aditi
systems.mechanism_summary: Aditi consists of DitA and DitB. The page assigns neither protein a resolved function and leaves the defense mechanism unknown.

systems.title: Avs

effector.value: Diverse effectors (Nucleic acid degrading, putative Nucleotide modifying, putative Membrane disrupting)

systems.mechanism_summary: Characterized Avs sensors recognize phage terminase or portal proteins, assemble into active complexes and stimulate diverse effectors, often DNA nucleases. The page warns that its mechanistic subtype numbering differs from the older DefenseFinder classification.

systems.title: Azaca
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies an Azaca genomic example with ZacA, ZacB and ZacC but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: Borvo
systems.mechanism_summary: Borvo is a one-protein defense. Phage polymerase escape mutations implicate the polymerase as a possible trigger, while abortive infection and the precise mechanism remain provisional.

systems.title: BREX
systems.mechanism_summary: BREX blocks phage replication and includes several gene architectures. Type I host-DNA methylation is linked to proposed self-recognition, but the page does not establish the downstream restriction mechanism or describe it as ordinary DNA cleavage.

systems.title: BstA
systems.mechanism_summary: BstA inhibits phage DNA replication and is proposed to cause abortive infection. The page describes a locus-specific anti-BstA element protecting the encoding prophage, while leaving the detailed defense mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Bunzi
systems.mechanism_summary: Bunzi contains BnzA and BnzB. Domain similarities are reported, but the wiki provides no resolved molecular mechanism.

systems.title: Butters_gp30_gp31
systems.mechanism_summary: This two-protein defense is proposed to couple a cytoplasmic sensor to a membrane channel, causing depolarization and ATP loss. The page identifies this as a Rex-like hypothesis, not an established mechanism.

systems.title: Butters_gp57r
systems.mechanism_summary: Butters_gp57r acts after phage DNA entry and inhibits subsequent DNA amplification. The page proposes participation of its HEPN domain without resolving the biochemical mechanism.

systems.title: CapRel
systems.mechanism_summary: CapRel combines toxin and regulatory regions in one protein. Phage capsid recognition releases inhibition of its toxin region, leading to transfer RNA pyrophosphorylation and blocked translation; homologs can differ in phage specificity.

systems.title: CARD_NLR
systems.mechanism_summary: CARD_NLR systems couple NLR-like ATPases and proteases to variable effectors. A characterized gasdermin-containing system damages the membrane; other architectures contain different candidate effectors, so the family does not imply one universal output.

systems.title: CRISPR-Cas
systems.mechanism_summary: CRISPR-Cas loci encode adaptive immunity in bacteria and archaea. The page supplies representative genomic architectures for six types; the embedded classification reference discusses modular evolution rather than a universal effector mechanism.

systems.title: CBASS

effector.value: Divers (Nucleic acid degrading, Nucleotide modifying, Membrane disrupting)

systems.mechanism_summary: CBASS uses cyclic-oligonucleotide signaling to activate defense. This page emphasizes membrane-disrupting examples, including Cap15, and provides four subtype architectures; that example-specific output is not a universal effector assignment.

systems.title: Charlie_gp32
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a Charlie_gp32 genomic example containing gp32 but does not describe its molecular mechanism.

systems.title: DarTG
systems.mechanism_summary: DarT modifies viral single-stranded DNA by ADP-ribosylation, impairing replication, while DarG reverses the modification. The page distinguishes this direct inhibition of phage replication from obligatory host-killing abortive infection.

systems.title: Dazbog
systems.mechanism_summary: Dazbog contains DzbA and DzbB. A domain similarity is reported for DzbA, but the page leaves the molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: dCTPdeaminase
systems.mechanism_summary: The defense reduces the available deoxycytidine nucleotide pool through deamination, limiting building blocks for phage DNA synthesis. The page describes infection-dependent activation without resolving all triggering steps.

systems.title: DdmDE
systems.mechanism_summary: The embedded reference reports that DdmDE cooperates with DdmABC to eliminate small multicopy plasmids. The page supplies a DdmD/E genomic example without assigning individual biochemical steps to those proteins.

systems.title: Detocs
systems.mechanism_summary: Detocs combines a sensor kinase, a receiver-only regulator and a receiver–effector protein. Characterized PNP effectors deplete adenine nucleotides; other effector types occur, and the downstream infection outcome varies by phage.

systems.title: dGTPase

sensor.value: Monitoring of the host cell machinery integrity

systems.mechanism_summary: Defensive dGTPase removes dGTP from the nucleotide pool by converting it to deoxyguanosine. Escape mutations suggest a link to phage-induced changes in host transcription, but the activation route remains provisional.

systems.title: DISARM
systems.mechanism_summary: DISARM couples DNA-modification-associated genes with a DrmAB DNA-binding complex and a candidate DrmC nuclease-domain protein. The page reports restriction and methylation-sensitive activation evidence but leaves the DNA-degradation mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Dnd
systems.mechanism_summary: Dnd gene clusters install sequence-selective phosphorothioate modifications in the DNA backbone. The page supplies Dnd_ABCDE and Dnd_ABCDEFGH examples; its embedded discovery reference establishes modification chemistry without detailing every restriction component.

systems.title: Dodola
systems.mechanism_summary: Dodola contains DolA and DolB, with DUF6414 and ClpB-like domains described respectively. The wiki leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Dpd
systems.mechanism_summary: Dpd-associated pathways introduce deazapurine derivatives into DNA. The embedded reference links modification-dependent plasmid transformation differences to a proposed restriction–modification role; it does not establish identical activity for every listed component.

systems.title: DRT
systems.mechanism_summary: DRT systems contain defense-associated reverse transcriptases in multiple architectures. The page distinguishes largely unresolved types from characterized DRT2 and DRT9, and explains a noncoding-RNA-dependent protein-production mechanism for DRT2.

systems.title: Druantia
systems.mechanism_summary: Druantia has three described architectures with different Dru protein complements. The wiki leaves the molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Dsr
systems.mechanism_summary: The characterized Dsr2 protein recognizes phage tail-tube components and activates NAD degradation, interrupting cellular and viral replication. A phage antagonist can prevent activation; this mechanism should not automatically be extended to every Dsr subtype.

systems.title: Eleos
systems.mechanism_summary: Eleos contains dynamin-like Leo proteins, either LeoA with LeoBC or separate LeoA/B/C proteins. Antiphage activity is reported, while the molecular mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: FS_GIY_YIG
systems.mechanism_summary: This one-protein defense contains a GIY-YIG endonuclease domain. Nucleic-acid degradation is proposed from domain evidence, but the page leaves the defense mechanism uncharacterized.

systems.title: FS_HEPN_TM
systems.mechanism_summary: FS_HEPN_TM contains a HEPN-domain protein and a predicted transmembrane partner. Antiphage protection is reported, but the molecular mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: FS_HP
systems.mechanism_summary: FS_HP is a one-protein defense reported to reduce phage production in both lytic and induced-prophage settings. The page provides no resolved molecular mechanism.

systems.title: FS_HP_SDH_sah
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies an FS_HP_SDH_sah genomic example with HP and SDH_sah proteins but does not explain its molecular mechanism.

systems.title: FS_HsdR_like
systems.mechanism_summary: FS_HsdR_like contains DUF6731, a hypothetical protein and a protein described with HEPN and zinc-finger regions. Antiphage and conjugation-blocking effects are reported, but the molecular mechanism is unresolved.

systems.title: FS_Sma
systems.mechanism_summary: SMA is a one-protein antiphage system with similarity to the MazF ribonuclease. The page describes the domain analogy without establishing that SMA uses the same biochemical mechanism.

systems.title: Gabija
systems.mechanism_summary: Gabija combines GajA-mediated DNA nicking with GajB nucleotide hydrolysis. The page proposes feedback between DNA-end sensing and nucleotide depletion while noting that the complete infection-response mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: Gao_Ape
systems.mechanism_summary: Gao_Ape contains the HEPN-family protein ApeA. Abortive infection is proposed, while the page leaves the molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Gao_Her
systems.mechanism_summary: Gao_Her couples HerA to Sir2- or DUF4297-associated effectors. ATP-dependent regulation can enable NAD depletion and, in some characterized systems, DNA degradation; the page distinguishes variable outcomes of growth arrest and cell death.

systems.title: Gao_Hhe
systems.mechanism_summary: Gao_Hhe contains HheA with predicted helicase and Vsr-like endonuclease domains. Antiphage activity is reported, but the molecular mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: Gao_Iet
systems.mechanism_summary: Gao_Iet contains the ATPase IetA and protease IetS. The page gives these protein annotations but leaves the defense mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Gao_Mza
systems.mechanism_summary: Gao_Mza comprises MzaA–E proteins and has reported antiphage activity. The page leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved; its genomic example includes a duplicated MzaE entry.

systems.title: Gao_Ppl
systems.mechanism_summary: Gao_Ppl is a one-protein defense with PHP and ATPase domains. A nuclease function is suggested by the PHP annotation, but the molecular defense mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: Gao_Qat
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a Gao_Qat example containing QatA, QatB, QatC and QatD, without a molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: Gao_RL
systems.mechanism_summary: Gao_RL contains RL_A–D proteins and is described as resembling restriction systems. The wiki leaves the molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Gao_TerY
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a Gao_TerY example with TerYA, TerYB and TerYC, without a molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: Gao_Tmn
systems.mechanism_summary: Gao_Tmn is a membrane-associated KAP-family NTPase. It can act alone or enhance defenses such as Gabija and Septu; amplification of ATPase signaling is proposed, while the detailed mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: Gao_Upx
systems.mechanism_summary: Gao_Upx is a one-protein defense identified in defense-associated genomic regions. The page reports experimental validation but leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: GAPS1
systems.mechanism_summary: GAPS1 activation is linked to a phage capsid protein. Its predicted nuclease domain is required for defense, but the cited experiments did not detect target-phage DNA degradation, leaving the molecular output unresolved.

systems.title: GAPS2
systems.mechanism_summary: GAPS2 is a one-protein defense with a reported BRCT domain. Its molecular mechanism remains unresolved on the wiki.

systems.title: GAPS4
systems.mechanism_summary: GAPS4 requires GAPS4a and GAPS4b. A predicted PD-(D/E)XK nuclease domain and infection-dependent host-DNA degradation support a proposed abortive-infection mechanism, with the reported degradation depending on the tested phage.

systems.title: GAPS6
systems.mechanism_summary: GAPS6 contains two proteins. GAPS6b includes TPR repeats and a predicted PIN ribonuclease domain required for defense, but its sufficiency and complete activation mechanism remain unresolved.

systems.title: GasderMIN
systems.mechanism_summary: Proteolytic removal of an inhibitory region activates bacterial gasdermins, allowing membrane-pore formation and cell death. The page describes associated proteases and recognition components as part of characterized defense contexts.

systems.title: Hachiman
systems.mechanism_summary: The page describes HamB helicase control of the HamA nuclease, with DNA damage and ATP hydrolysis releasing DNA-cleavage activity. It also retains a general unknown-mechanism sentence, so its statements are internally inconsistent in certainty.

systems.title: Hna
systems.mechanism_summary: Hna contains helicase- and nuclease-associated motifs required for defense in the reported tests. The embedded reference describes abortive infection triggered by a phage single-stranded-DNA-binding protein, without fully resolving the biochemical sequence.

systems.title: ISG15-like
systems.mechanism_summary: ISG15-like defenses contain BilA–D proteins. Conjugation of the ubiquitin-like BilA to phage tail components disrupts tail assembly or function, producing progeny with reduced infectivity.

systems.title: JukAB
systems.mechanism_summary: JukA detects an early jumbo-phage infection structure and recruits JukB. The proposed disruption of phage protection exposes DNA to other host nucleases; the page does not identify JukA or JukB themselves as the DNA-cleaving enzyme.

systems.title: Kiwa
systems.mechanism_summary: Kiwa couples membrane sensor KwaA to DNA-binding KwaB. Following phage attachment, the complex inhibits phage replication and late transcription without reported DNA degradation; some activation steps remain unresolved.

systems.title: Lamassu-Fam

effector.value: Diverse (Nucleic acid degrading (?), Nucleotide modifying (?), Membrane disrupting (?))

systems.mechanism_summary: Lamassu systems combine an SMC-like component with variable effectors and often an accessory protein. The page describes abortive-infection and antiplasmid examples, including a hairpin-DNA-triggered system, without resolving a universal family mechanism.

systems.title: Lit

effector.value: Other (Cleaves an elongation factor, inhibiting cellular translation

systems.mechanism_summary: Phage capsid binding to EF-Tu enables Lit-mediated cleavage of that translation factor. Translation arrest and cell death interrupt phage production late in infection.

systems.title: MADS
systems.mechanism_summary: MADS is a methylation-associated defense reported to cooperate with type I-E CRISPR-Cas against anti-CRISPR-bearing phages. The embedded reference describes this combined protection; the page does not explain the individual MADS proteins mechanistically.

systems.title: MazEF
systems.mechanism_summary: MazEF pairs the stable MazF toxin with a less stable MazE antitoxin. The embedded reference reports reduced P1 production and population protection associated with toxin-dependent death, without detailing the toxin chemistry on this page.

systems.title: Menshen
systems.mechanism_summary: Menshen contains NsnA, NsnB and NsnC and has reported antiphage activity. The wiki leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: MMB_gp29_gp30
systems.mechanism_summary: This prophage-associated two-protein system protects against some lytic infections without the reported abortive-infection phenotype. The page notes gp29 toxicity and frequent lysogeny among survivors, while leaving the mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Mok_Hok_Sok

sensor.value: Monitoring of the host cell machinery (?)

systems.mechanism_summary: The Sok RNA antitoxin restrains Hok toxicity, with Mok supporting Hok expression. During described T4 infection, reduced antitoxin availability allows membrane-depolarizing Hok activity and premature host death.

systems.title: Mokosh
systems.mechanism_summary: Mokosh combines RNA-helicase and PLD-nuclease-associated domains in separate or fused proteins. Mutating candidate catalytic regions disrupts defense, but the wiki does not resolve the full molecular mechanism.

systems.title: MqsRAC
systems.mechanism_summary: MqsRAC is described as a toxin–antitoxin–chaperone defense. Its embedded reference reports reversible persistence and cooperation with restriction systems during T2 infection, while the page leaves the detailed molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Nhi
systems.mechanism_summary: Nhi combines nuclease and helicase activities to attack phage replication intermediates. The page distinguishes clades recognizing single-stranded-DNA-binding proteins or replication initiators, while leaving triggers for other clades unresolved.
contributors: Alba Herrero del Valle, Andrew Berti

systems.title: NixI
systems.mechanism_summary: NixI produces sequence-specific nicks in the ICP1 phage genome, interfering with its transition to rolling-circle replication. The page distinguishes this activity from double-strand-break formation.

systems.title: NLR
systems.mechanism_summary: Bacterial NLR/bNACHT proteins combine a sensor, central NACHT module and variable effector region. The page describes this architecture while leaving the detailed activation and defense mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Old_exonuclease
systems.mechanism_summary: Characterized OLD proteins have ATPase-associated nuclease activity, including directional DNA degradation. The page links a prophage example to RecBCD inhibition while leaving other aspects of the family mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Olokun
systems.mechanism_summary: Olokun contains OloA and OloB, with adaptin-associated and nuclease-domain annotations respectively. Antiphage activity is reported, but the page leaves the molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: pAgo
systems.mechanism_summary: Prokaryotic Argonautes use nucleic-acid guides to recognize targets. Some long-A proteins cleave targets, whereas catalytically inactive forms can activate accessory effectors; the page describes multiple outputs, including nuclease activity, NAD depletion and membrane disruption.

systems.title: Panchino_gp28
systems.mechanism_summary: The page describes prophage-encoded Panchino gp28 as a one-gene type I restriction system. It provides no further biochemical mechanism details.

systems.title: Paris
systems.mechanism_summary: PARIS combines ATPase-associated AriA and DUF4435-associated AriB, either separate or fused. Recognition of the phage anti-restriction protein Ocr triggers growth arrest, while the downstream mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: PD-Lambda-1
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-Lambda-1 is a one-protein defense reported to protect against LambdaVir. Its molecular mechanism remains unresolved on the wiki.

systems.title: PD-Lambda-2
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a PD-Lambda-2 example containing three named proteins but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: PD-Lambda-3
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-Lambda-3 is a two-protein defense discovered through an experimental screen. The page leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: PD-Lambda-4
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a two-protein PD-Lambda-4 genomic example but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: PD-Lambda-5
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-Lambda-5 pairs a nuclease/HEPN-associated protein with a predicted methyltransferase. The page reports broad protection without a clear abortive-infection phenotype and leaves the molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: PD-Lambda-6
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a one-protein PD-Lambda-6 genomic example but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: PD-T4-1
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a one-protein PD-T4-1 genomic example but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: PD-T4-10
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-T4-10 contains overlapping genes whose products show toxin and toxicity-neutralizing activities. The page proposes toxin–antitoxin control of abortive infection but leaves the biochemical mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: PD-T4-2
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a two-protein PD-T4-2 genomic example but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: PD-T4-3
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-T4-3 is a one-protein defense requiring an intact GIY-YIG-associated region for resistance. The page reports this functional dependency while leaving the molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: PD-T4-4
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-T4-4 contains proteins annotated as a P-loop NTPase and nuclease. Abortive infection is proposed, while the molecular mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: PD-T4-5
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a one-protein PD-T4-5 genomic example but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: PD-T4-6
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-T4-6 is a one-protein abortive-infection defense with a predicted kinase-associated region required for full protection. The wiki leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: PD-T4-7
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-T4-7 is a one-protein system reported to act through abortive infection. The page provides domain annotations and phage protection examples but no detailed biochemical mechanism.

systems.title: PD-T4-8
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-T4-8 is a one-protein defense containing DUF4263, a domain also reported in Shedu. The page leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: PD-T4-9
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-T4-9, described as CmdTAC, contains a modifying toxin, antitoxin and chaperone. Phage capsid interaction changes antitoxin control and enables toxin-dependent RNA modification, disrupting translation.

systems.title: PD-T7-1
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-T7-1 is a one-protein defense with reported protection against T7. Its molecular mechanism remains unresolved on the wiki.

systems.title: PD-T7-2
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a two-protein PD-T7-2 genomic example but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: PD-T7-3
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-T7-3 is a one-protein defense discovered in an experimental screen. The wiki leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: PD-T7-4
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a one-protein PD-T7-4 genomic example but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: PD-T7-5
systems.mechanism_summary: PD-T7-5 has reported antiphage activity and a PD-(D/E)XK-associated domain. DNA degradation is proposed from this annotation, while the molecular mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: PfiAT
systems.mechanism_summary: PfiAT regulates the Pf4 prophage through a toxin–antitoxin complex affecting transcription. The page explicitly questions whether it should be classified as an antiphage defense system.

systems.title: Phrann_gp29_gp30
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a gp29/gp30 example. Its embedded discovery reference links Phrann-associated defense to a predicted alarmone synthetase and inhibition of phage growth, while not resolving the individual roles of both proteins here.

systems.title: Pif
systems.mechanism_summary: PifA mediates abortive infection through increased membrane permeability and consequent nucleotide loss. The page presents the defense in the context of F-factor-associated phage inhibition.

systems.title: PrrC

sensor.value: Monitor the integrity of the bacterial cell machinery

systems.mechanism_summary: PrrC acts with a type I restriction–modification system. Phage-mediated inhibition of that partner can activate PrrC cleavage of lysine transfer RNA, interrupting translation and phage growth.

systems.title: PsyrTA
systems.mechanism_summary: PsyrTA pairs a toxin associated with helicase and phosphoribosyltransferase annotations with a nucleotide-binding antitoxin. The page supplies domain-based context but not a complete biochemical defense mechanism.

systems.title: Pycsar
systems.mechanism_summary: Pycsar cyclases produce cyclic pyrimidine nucleotide signals that activate diverse cell-killing effectors. Phage Apyc proteins can degrade these signals and suppress the defense response.

systems.title: RADAR
systems.mechanism_summary: RADAR combines RdrA ATPase and RdrB deaminase activities. The page distinguishes initial RNA-editing observations from later ATP-deamination evidence, with accumulation of inosine nucleotides implicated in restricting phage replication.

systems.title: Retron

sensor.value: Monitor the integrity of the bacterial cell machinery

systems.mechanism_summary: Defensive retrons combine reverse transcriptase, noncoding RNA and an effector. Their DNA/RNA product participates in subtype-specific regulation; the page describes both monitored host processes and toxin–antitoxin mechanisms rather than one universal output.

systems.title: RexAB
systems.mechanism_summary: RexAB excludes phages through a response involving ATP loss, impaired transport and cell death. The embedded reference proposes that membrane-associated RexB forms channels causing depolarization; it distinguishes this model from a fully resolved mechanism.

systems.title: RloC

sensor.value: Monitor the integrity of the bacterial cell machinery

systems.mechanism_summary: RloC has demonstrated transfer-RNA-cleaving activity and regulatory ATPase/zinc-hook features. The page explicitly states that antiphage activity was not experimentally established there; defense assignment is based on similarity and genomic context.

systems.title: RM
systems.mechanism_summary: Typical restriction–modification systems distinguish DNA through modification state and couple restriction activity with protective methylation. The page also includes separate type I, II, IIG, III and IV genomic examples, whose architectures should not be treated as interchangeable.

systems.title: RnlAB

sensor.value: Monitor the integrity of the bacterial cell machinery

systems.mechanism_summary: RnlAB pairs an RNA-cleaving RnlA toxin with the RnlB antitoxin, which suppresses that activity.

systems.title: RosmerTA
systems.mechanism_summary: RosmerTA contains a zinc-peptidase-associated protein and a variable toxin. Membrane depolarization is reported for one representative, without establishing that output for every family member.

systems.title: Rst_2TM_1TM_TIR
systems.mechanism_summary: This three-protein system contains a TIR-domain protein and membrane-associated partners. A TIR-derived nucleotide signal activating the membrane proteins is proposed, while the molecular mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: Rst_3HP
systems.mechanism_summary: Rst_3HP contains Hp1, Hp2 and Hp3 with no clear domain assignments. Antiphage resistance is reported, but the molecular mechanism is unresolved.

systems.title: Rst_DUF4238
systems.mechanism_summary: Rst_DUF4238 is a one-protein defense with reported T7 resistance. The page leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Rst_gop_beta_cll
systems.mechanism_summary: Rst_gop_beta_cll contains gop, beta and cll. Toxicity from gop without beta suggests toxin–antitoxin regulation, but the page leaves the defense mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Rst_HelicaseDUF2290
systems.mechanism_summary: Rst_HelicaseDUF2290 pairs a helicase-associated protein with a DUF2290 protein. The page leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Rst_Hydrolase-3Tm
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a hydrolase-associated and membrane-associated two-protein example but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: Rst_RT-nitrilase-Tm
systems.mechanism_summary: Rst_RT-nitrilase-Tm pairs a reverse-transcriptase/nitrilase-associated protein with a membrane protein. Antiphage activity is reported, while the molecular mechanism remains unresolved.

systems.title: Rst_TIR-NLR
systems.mechanism_summary: Rst_TIR-NLR contains a protein with TIR- and NLR-associated regions. The page notes related defense families but leaves this system's molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: SanaTA
systems.mechanism_summary: SanaTA pairs a nucleotidyltransferase-associated toxin with an antitoxin. The page links defense to Lon-mediated antitoxin degradation, releasing toxin activity in the tested infection context.

systems.title: SEFIR
systems.mechanism_summary: The characterized bacterial SEFIR defense depletes NAD and causes abortive infection. The page relates this activity to other STIR-superfamily defenses without making the domain alone proof of activity in a query protein.

systems.title: Septu
systems.mechanism_summary: Septu combines PtuA with the PtuB HNH nuclease. ATP inhibits the characterized complex's DNA-cleaving activity; infection-driven ATP depletion is proposed to activate it. The page also notes reverse-transcriptase-containing related architectures.

systems.title: Shango
systems.mechanism_summary: Shango requires TerB-associated, helicase and ATPase components. Their functional importance is reported, while membrane surveillance remains a proposed explanation for an unresolved defense mechanism.

systems.title: Shedu
systems.mechanism_summary: Shedu proteins contain a PD-(D/E)XK-associated nuclease region with variable regulatory regions. Characterized examples show infection-linked assembly or DNA-end recognition controlling DNA cleavage; their sensing mechanisms are not identical.

systems.title: ShosTA
systems.mechanism_summary: ShosTA couples a purine-metabolism-disrupting toxin to a DNA-repair-associated antitoxin. The page describes phage-triggered loss of antitoxin protection and ensuing toxin activity, while some neutralization steps remain proposed.

systems.title: SoFIC
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a one-protein SoFIC genomic example but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: SpbK
systems.mechanism_summary: SpbK is a TIR-domain protein reported to protect against a temperate phage. The embedded reference links expression with the phage protein YonE to abortive infection, without detailing the downstream biochemistry.

systems.title: SspBCDE
systems.mechanism_summary: Ssp phosphorothioate modification can pair with SspE or SspFGH defense. The embedded reference describes SspE-dependent nucleotide hydrolysis and DNA nicking, and SspFGH damage to unmodified DNA; the two restriction modules can coexist with one modification module.

systems.title: Stk2
systems.mechanism_summary: Stk2 is a serine/threonine kinase activated by a phage protein called Pack. Broad phosphorylation of essential cellular processes is proposed to cause the observed abortive-infection response.

systems.title: Thoeris
systems.mechanism_summary: Thoeris couples TIR-associated ThsB sensing and signaling to ThsA NADase activity. The described cyclic ADP-ribose-related signal activates NAD depletion, suppressing infected-cell growth and phage propagation.

systems.title: Tiamat
systems.mechanism_summary: Tiamat is a one-protein TmtA defense with reported antiphage activity. The wiki leaves its molecular mechanism unresolved.

systems.title: Uzume
systems.mechanism_summary: The page supplies a one-protein Uzume example containing UzuA but no molecular-mechanism explanation.

systems.title: Viperin
systems.mechanism_summary: Prokaryotic viperins use radical-SAM chemistry to generate modified ribonucleotides. Their incorporation can terminate viral RNA synthesis; different viperins can use different nucleotide substrates.

systems.title: Wadjet
systems.mechanism_summary: Wadjet combines a JetABC DNA-topology-sensing complex with JetD nuclease activity. The page describes defense against circular plasmid DNA, with JetD-dependent cleavage requiring the partner complex, rather than demonstrated antiphage activity.

source_issue_details.explanation: The wiki cites a 2005 review of general SMC chromosome mechanics for Wadjet-specific cleavage and topology statements. The original citation is retained but is not accepted here as independently verified direct support for those statements. Its use for general Muk/SMC similarity on line 27 is outside this flag.

bibliographic_check.title: SMC proteins and chromosome mechanics: from bacteria to humans
bibliographic_check.author: Tatsuya Hirano

systems.title: Zorya
systems.mechanism_summary: In characterized type I Zorya, membrane-associated ZorAB is proposed to transmit an infection signal to DNA-binding ZorC/D and the ZorD nuclease. Other types have different additional components, so this mechanism is subtype-specific.
